hypothesis: After an exact HYPE-breakout-provider lifecycle first reaches 25, 40, or 60 bps maximum favorable excursion, requiring five causal weak-support decisions and then exiting at the next open after a completed-bar retrace to approximately +5 bps net may prevent profitable breakouts from turning into losses without prematurely closing sustained continuations.
decision: Retain the challenger as report-only negative evidence and do not alter v14 or v18 execution. All three predeclared activation arms reduced mean after-cost return versus the actual live exits. The 40-bps arm was least harmful and protected isolated losing paths, but it still surrendered 34.72 mean bps across the ten exact-provider lifecycles and 40.44 mean bps on the nine native-HYPE lifecycles. Weak support or RANGE is therefore insufficient exit authority; any later challenger must require genuine directional opposition or a harder price failure and must be tested prospectively.
falsifier: This rejection would be updated by a larger prospective exact-provider sample in which a frozen arm improves total and mean net return after measured friction, does not materially reduce the right tail, remains directionally symmetric, and holds across more than one profile generation. A single protected loser or one currently open lifecycle does not falsify the rejection.
limitations: The hypothesis was specified after observing favorable-excursion giveback, so this is retrospective mechanism evidence rather than a sealed prospective test.
Only ten resolved exact-provider lifecycles exist and nine are native HYPE; this is enough to reject immediate promotion but not to estimate a stable future effect.
The counterfactual reuses each actual exit fill/reference ratio and fee rate; it cannot reproduce private queue state or the exact IOC book at an earlier timestamp.
Profile generations, sizing, and leverage differ, so results are normalized in basis points and are not a shared-portfolio equity replay.
The currently open v14 HYPE lifecycle is excluded until resolved and cannot be used as completed outcome evidence.
No live strategy, position, order, stop, backend process, configuration, or execution authority changed in this experiment.
